title: Salsa Dip 450g

drivers.name: Promotion: 20% off
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted promotion lift from 15 past events is x1.36; this 20% discount is shallower than prior 25-30% off events, which had higher lifts (x1.97, x3.1). No seasonality support.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is similar in size to past promotions (25% off, 30% off), but the 30% off event had an outlier lift (x3.1) due to back-to-school season. The noise-adjusted lift from 15 past promotions is x1.36, but this week's 20% discount is less aggressive. The classical model's x1.36 is a reasonable starting point, but we adjust down due to lower discount depth and absence of seasonal tailwind. The same week after past promotions shows a 7% dip (x0.93), but no evidence of pantry loading here. No other drivers. Evidence is moderate, so shrink toward 1.0.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-28% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
